proof.observed: settleAndRecord (publisher.go:271-306) returns without writing on exactly one path, line 293, which first sets result.fenced = true; that path is also taken whenever result.fenced was already true. Every other return wrote (recordBatch at 303). So after each call, 'not written' == result.fenced. The two former readers: settleOwner (320-333) checks err first, then result.fenced where it checked !done.wrote; the batch end (387-395) checks err first, then result.fenced. A failed write (wrote was true, err set) takes the err branch first in both, before and after, so it is unchanged; a fenced batch returns err nil and is caught by result.fenced. settleOwner is called only from sendChains' settle/finish on its one goroutine (batch.go:523-612, an unlocked inflight slice), so result.fenced cannot change between a call and its read. No reader of wrote remains (rg).
